benchmark: water-rs/waterui#1262 competitive benchmark — iOS on a physical iPhone

device.note: the one Apple benchmark platform; macOS and the iOS Simulator are not benchmark platforms. device_state() refuses a device whose devicectl product type differs.

build_host.water_cli: in-tree waterui-cli (cli/ is a workspace member of this checkout): `cargo install --locked --path cli` into the suite .cache once per host; framework+CLI+backend identity = checkout HEAD sha, recorded in the staging manifest

toolchain.xcode: not pinned: every host records the Xcode it actually uses (xcodebuild -version, iphoneos SDK version and build) — the build host in the staging manifest, the device host in the results — and must report exactly one Xcode

bootstrap.note: build host only. Fresh-clone dependency install, pinned to committed lockfiles: the RN init template is materialized first (lib/toolchain.ensure_rn_template); npm ci installs exactly package-lock.json; bundle install honors Gemfile.lock; pod install runs as `pod _<version>_ install` with the toolchain.build_host.cocoapods pin (the generated RN Gemfile caps CocoaPods at 1.15.2 via xcodeproj < 1.26.0, so `bundle exec pod` can never reach it); xcodegen generates native-bench/NativeBench.xcodeproj from the committed project.yml (the generated project is not committed). The whole bootstrap runs inside lib/toolchain.tracked_tree_unchanged.

w5.name: Motion capacity: W3 scene, rects 200→25600 doubling

w6.name: Feed capacity: W2 fling over rows ×1→64 nested children

contestants.label: WaterUI — Rust/objc2 apple backend
contestants.framework_version: waterui @ checkout HEAD — framework, cli, apple backend and hydrolysis are all workspace members of this checkout

contestants.label: SwiftUI
contestants.framework_version: iOS SDK of the build host's Xcode (system; recorded in the staging manifest)
build: cd native-bench && xcodebuild -project NativeBench.xcodeproj -scheme BenchApps -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -derivedDataPath build/dd CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build

contestants.label: UIKit
contestants.framework_version: iOS SDK of the build host's Xcode (system; recorded in the staging manifest)

contestants.label: React Native
build: cd ../apps/react-native && LANG=en_US.UTF-8 xcodebuild -workspace ios/RnBench.xcworkspace -scheme RnBench -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -derivedDataPath build/dd CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build

runner.note: the XCTest UI runner (xctest/project.yml) is built on the device host with its Xcode; its app is <bundle_id>.xctrunner, the bundle id the device host needs a profile for

signing.note: device host only. Each contestant's `bundle_id` above is the id the device host signs it as (CFBundleIdentifier is set on the signed copy; the staged artifact keeps its built id): distinct ids per contestant, or one id shared by several contestants — the device host installs one contestant at a time and uninstalls it before the next, so a shared id never has two apps installed. Every id needs a profile on the device host whose App ID is exactly <team>.<id> (never a wildcard), that includes the host's one Apple Development certificate and the device, valid for profile_min_validity_h; a missing one fails the run naming the id and how to create it (Xcode automatic signing for that id). A free personal team's profiles are per id and expire after 7 days; the team may register 10 App IDs per 7 days and have 3 of its apps installed on a device at once (here: the runner + the contestant under measurement).

harness.warmup_note: declared warmup, never 0 — METHOD (../WORKLOADS.md): the window is [first owned present + harness.warmup_ms, + duration_s], computed on the all-process Animation Hitches device trace, where a present is owned when the frame's (display, swap) composited an update from a process inside the contestant's bundle; readiness is that first owned present. The trace is readable only after the recording stops, so dev.bench.ready is the live signal a drive starts on: the runner starts the drive at ready + warmup and marks it with a dev.bench drive-begin Points of Interest signpost in the same trace.
harness.anchor_tolerance_note: for a driven cell (tap, swipe) the drive-begin signpost must lie within this many ms of the trace's window start (METHOD: the drive starts at window start), else the row fails; an undriven cell (w3, w5) records its offset ungated. The runner also holds the contestant this long past the capture, so the window end lies inside the held span whenever the drive offset is in tolerance. Every row records window.drive_offset_ms; the value is provisional until the first device reps show the real ready-to-first-present spread per contestant (RN and Flutter present a launch view before their ready post).

fling.note: XCUICoordinate press-and-drag from start_fraction to end_fraction of the app's height over duration_ms (velocity = distance / duration), after a hold_s press; pause_ms between flings — WORKLOADS.md shared fling protocol

disk.note: free bytes the device host's run dir must have before each cell starts its one recording (Animation Hitches + Points of Interest + os_log: its .trace bundle and the Instruments raw ktrace scratch the cell removes before the next cell starts); a cell short of it fails with the free byte count. Every row records disk_free_bytes, trace_bytes and the removed scratch bytes, so the floor is re-derived from the first device recordings.

measurement.method: shared XCUITest runner + XCTest metrics (XCTApplicationLaunchMetric, XCTMemoryMetric, XCTCPUMetric, XCTHitchMetric, XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollingAndDecelerationMetric on w2/w4/w6) + one all-process xctrace recording per launch on the device (Animation Hitches + Points of Interest + os_log: frames, the runner's marks, time-sample CPU of the app and backboardd, and the WaterUI first-paint marker)
measurement.order: contestants interleaved across repeats; one discarded launch-test warm-up per contestant per results file
measurement.launch_arg: -bench-workload w1|w2|w3|w4|w5|w6 -bench-step N (w5/w6; N is the ladder value; one launch renders one step) — single dash; NSArgumentDomain/UserDefaults. Workload ids are exact lowercase strings; a missing or unrecognized value traps naming the argument, and the app posts dev.bench.ready.<its CFBundleIdentifier>.<w> when the workload view first appears (SwiftUI onAppear, UIKit viewDidAppear, WaterUI on_appear, Flutter's first frame of the workload page, React Native's first content appearance).
measurement.package_size: build host: the unsigned arm64 .app bytes on disk and the deflated Payload/ zip of it (the unsigned .ipa); device host: the thinned .ipa for the measured device's variant (xcodebuild -exportArchive with exportOptions thinning = the device product type) — its bytes (download, compressed) and the sum of its entries (installed, uncompressed), with Xcode's App Thinning Size Report line as evidence

notes: BUILD IDENTITY: the WaterUI contestant is the Rust + objc2 apple backend at checkout HEAD, packaged by the in-tree cli/ built from this checkout (`water package --platform ios --backend apple --release --unsigned`: CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO, static Rust in the main executable). The device host refuses a staged set built at another HEAD than its own checkout.

Swipe gestures are raw XCUICoordinate press/drag HID events — app.swipeUp() resolves 'descendants matching type Window' plus a per-gesture quiescence wait that stalls past 117 s on a scrolling 10k-row list.
XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollingAndDecelerationMetric is attached only for w2/w4/w6 (it emits zero rows on w1/w3).
W2 idioms: React Native uses Animated.FlatList (windowing + view recycling); UIKit dequeueReusableCell; SwiftUI List; Flutter ListView.builder.

Thermal gate: the runner's setUp blocks on ProcessInfo.thermalStateDidChangeNotification until the device is nominal and fails the row past its bound; thermal state and screen maximumFramesPerSecond are recorded per row from the runner log (device-record) — devicectl reports neither.

RnBench: only authored files are committed (AppDelegate.swift, bridging header, Info.plist, project.pbxproj, Podfile, Podfile.lock); every template file the pinned @react-native-community/cli init emits is materialized by toolchain.ensure_rn_template at bootstrap and sha256-locked.
